items.title: Larry Ridley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 10, 2003
items.q: He got a job in the plants during the war at Allison Motor Company, you know they make the engines for the airplanes.

ctx.x: was some of the stuff that early people say oh that music was born in the brothels and houses of ill repute. And it’s funny because when I first started saying I wanted to play jazz I told my father that I wanted to play jazz, because he liked that I was playing the violin, and he said, “Oh I don’t particularly like the idea of you playing jazz because you’ll be in those clubs where all those people are drinking and this, that and the other.” I said, “Daddy, that’s not why I want to play jazz. Because this is a…

Guess what? A man with this kind of knowledge. He went around to the machines and was a chip collector. Putting it in — you know, cleaning up. Because they wouldn’t hire him because of his color. You know that kind of craziness. I mean here’s a man, who knows what he could have contributed if he had been given the opportunity. That’s why I try to tell the young African-American kids now — you don’t realize the dues that people paid. And this whole thing about getting out to vote? Hey, I came up through that…
